$\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$
As the reaction is accompanied by decrease in randomness,

For reaction to be spontaneous $\Delta G$ should be

According to the new Cartesian sign conventions, magnification for a convex mirror is positive because image formed by a convex mirror is always virtual and erect. 1782.subject: Physics
1782.text: The focal length of the objective and eye lenses of a microscope are \(1.6 \mathrm{~cm}\) and \(2.5 \mathrm{~cm}\) respectively. The distance between the two lenses is \(21.7 \mathrm{~cm}\). If the final image is formed at infinity. What is the linear magnification?
1782.sol:
Here \(v_O=L-f_e=21.7 \mathrm{ cm}-2.5 \mathrm{ cm}=+19.2 \mathrm{ cm}\) \(+v e\) sign shows that image is real.
For a objective lens \(\frac{1}{u_O}+\frac{1}{v_O}=\frac{1}{f_O}\)
[using real-virtual sign convention]
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \frac{1}{u_O}=\frac{1}{f_O}-\frac{1}{v_O} \quad \therefore \quad \frac{1}{u_O}=\frac{1}{(+1.6)}-\frac{1}{(+19.2)} \\
& \frac{1}{u_O}=\frac{19.2-1.6}{(1.6)(19.2)} \quad \text{$ or $} \quad u_O=+1.745 \mathrm{ cm}
\end{aligned}\)
+ve sign shows that object is real.
When the image is formed at infinity, the magnification is given by
\(m=\left(\frac{v_O}{u_O}\right)\left(\frac{D}{f_e}\right)\)
where \(D\) is the distance of distinct vision.
\(\therefore \quad m=\left(\frac{19.2 \mathrm{ cm}}{1.745 \mathrm{ cm}}\right)\left(\frac{25 \mathrm{ cm}}{2.5 \mathrm{ cm}}\right)=110 .\)$

1977.subject: Zoology
1977.text: Which of the following match is correct?
options: Emphysema : reduction of surface area of alveoli and bronchi
Asthma : excessive secretion of bronchial mucus
1977.sol: Emphysema means abnormal accumulation of air in the tissues (lungs). In pulmonary emphysema the air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs are enlarged and damaged, which reduces the surface area for the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide. Severe emphysema causes breath-lessness, which is made worse by infections. Pneumonia is inflammation of the lung caused by bacteria, in which the air sacs (alveoli) become filled with inflammatory cells and the lung becomes solid. The symptoms include those of any infection (fever, malaise, headaches, etc.), together with cough and chest pain. Silicosis, a lung disease, is a form of pneumoconiosis produced by inhaling silica dust particles. It affects workers in hard-rock mining and tunnelling, quarrying, stone dressing, sand blasting, and boiler scaling. Silica stimulates fibrosis of lung tissue, which produces progressive breathlessness and considerebly increased susceptibility to tuberculosis. Asthma is the condition of subjects with widespread narrowing of the bronchial airways, which changes in severity over short periods of time (either spontaneously or under treatment) and leads to cough, wheezing, and difficulty in breathing.

1989.text: Which of the following pairs of hormones can easily pass through the cell membrane and binds to a receptor inside it (mostly in the nucleus)?
1989.sol: Cortisol and testosterone are steroidal in nature. Steroid hormones are lipid soluble and easily pass through cell membrane of a target cell into the cytoplasm. 2207.subject: Zoology
2207.text:
Assertion : Appetency is the formation of new structure or habit of the organism according to its need.
Reason : Appetency is also called doctrine of desire.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
2207.sol: According to Lamarck, a change in environment brings about changes in organisms. It gives rise to new needs. New needs or desires produce new structures and change habits of the organisms. Doctrine of desire is called appetency. It can be shown by the following example- Water birds (duck etc.) developed their webbed feet by constant stretching of digits and the skin between them for skimming the water surface and for swimming. The transmission of acquired characters is the most important principle usually termed as the Lamarckian doctrine.
2207.meta: Assertion : Appetency is the formation of new structure or habit of the organism according to its need. Reason : Appetency is also called doctrine of desire.

2228.subject: Zoology
2228.text:
Assertion : Fig and wasp cannot complete their life cycle without each other.
Reason : They show mutualistic relationship.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
2228.sol: In many species of fig trees, there is a tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp. It means that a given fig species can be pollinated only by its 'partner' wasp species and no other species. The female wasp uses the fruit not only as an oviposition (egg-laying) site but uses the developing seeds within the fruit for nourishing its larvae. The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg-laying sites. In return for the favour of pollination the fig offers the wasp some of its developing seeds, as food for the developing wasp larvae.
2228.meta: Assertion : Fig and wasp cannot complete their life cycle without each other. Reason : They show mutualistic relationship.

3419.subject: Chemistry
3419.text: Which of the following is correct related to the colours of ${TiCl}_{3}  \left(X\right) \left[Ti   \left({H}_{2}$ O\right)^{6}\right]{Cl}_{3}$\left(Y\right)$
3419.sol:
Atomic number of Titanium is 22.

Electronic configuration of Ti is& $\left[Ar\right]3d^{2}4s^{2}$

The colour of transition metal compounds is due to the presence of unpaired electrons in their metal ions which are responsible for d-d transitions.

The colour in the coordination compounds can be readily explained in terms of the crystal field theory. Consider, for example, the complex [Ti(H2O)6 ]3+, which is violet in colour. This is an octahedral complex where the single electron (Ti3+ is a 3d1 system) in the metal d orbital is in the t2g level in the ground state of the complex. The next higher state available for the electron is the empty eg level. If light corresponding to the energy of blue-green region is absorbed by the complex, it would excite the electron from t2g level to the eg level (t2g1 eg0 → t2g 0 eg1 ). Consequently, the complex appears violet in colour. The crystal field theory attributes the colour of the coordination compounds to d-d transition of the electron.

It is important to note that in the absence of ligand, crystal field splitting does not occur and hence the substance is colourless. For example, removal of water from [Ti(H2O)6 ]Cl3 on heating renders it colourless.Hence TiCl3& is colourless.

4684.text: Calculate the mass of $AgCl$ precipitated, when $25ml$ of $35 %$ solution of ${AgNO}_{3}$ and $25ml$ of $11. 6 %$ solution of $NaCl$ are mixed is
4684.sol:
${AgNO}_{3 ( aq )} + {NaCl}_{( aq )} \to {AgCl}_{( s )} + {NaNO}_{3 ( aq )}$

The above equation is balanced, and we can see that when one mole of ${AgNO}_{3}$ and one mole of $NaCl$ react then one mole of $AgCl$ is precipitated.

So, the reactant which is present in lesser quantity determines the amount of $AgCl$ formed.

$25ml$ of $35 % {AgNO}_{3}$

$= 25 \times \dfrac{35}{100} = 8. 75g$ of ${AgNO}_{3}$

$25ml$ of $11. 6 % NaCl$

$= 25 \times \dfrac{11. 6}{100} = 2. 9g$ of $NaCl$

As $1$ mole $NaCl = 58. 5g$

So, $2. 9g$ of $NaCl = \dfrac{2. 9}{58. 5} = 0. 049$ moles

Therefore, $0. 049$ moles of $AgCl$ is precipitated.

Hence, amount of $AgCl = numberofmoles \times molarmassofAgCl = 0. 049 \times 143g = 7g$

&

8081.text: Which one of the following is a linear differential equation?
8081.sol:
The standard form of linear differential equation is
$P \frac{d y}{d x}+Q y=R$ or $P \frac{d x}{d y}+Q x=R$ where $P, Q and R$ are the function of $x$ only.
Option (d) can be written as
$\begin{aligned} & x^2 d y+x y d x-d x=0 \\ & x^2 \frac{d y}{d x}+x y-1=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2 \frac{d y}{d x}+x y=1\end{aligned}$
Which follows the standard form of linear differential equation.

8588.sol:
As we know coordinates of circumcentre of an equilateral triangle is same as centroid, so

& $\text{$ and $} \quad \frac{3 m}{b}=\sin \theta_$1+\sin \theta_2+\sin \theta_3 \quad \ldots $\text{ (ii) }
\end{aligned}$
Now, after squaring and adding the Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

& \Rightarrow $\frac{9 l^2}{a^2}+\frac{9 m^2}{b^2}=$3+2 \Sigma \sin \theta_1 \sin \theta_2 \\
& \Rightarrow $\frac{2}{3} \Sigma \cos \left(\theta_$1-\theta_2\right)=$\frac{3 l^2}{a^2}+\frac{3 m^2}{b^2}-$1 \\
& \Rightarrow $\frac{2}{3}\left[\cos \left(\theta_$1-\theta_2\right)+\cos $\left(\theta_$2-\theta_3\right)+\cos $\left(\theta_$3-\theta_1\right)\right] \\
& =$\frac{3 l^2}{a^2}+\frac{3 m^2}{b^2}-$1
\end{aligned}\)

9367.sol:
Given, $\int x^3 \cdot e^{2 x} d x=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8} f(x)+c$ By applying integration by parts, we get $\begin{aligned}& \left.x^3 \cdot \inte^{2 x} d x-\int\left(\frac{d}{d x}x^3 \inte^{2 x} d x\right) d x\right)=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8}+f(x)+c \\
& x³ \cdot \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}-\int3 x² \cdot \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}d x=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8}f(x)+c \\
& \frac{1}{2}x^3 e^{2 x}-\frac{3}{2}\left[x^2 \cdot \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}-\int2 x \cdot \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}d x\right]=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8}f(x)+c
\end{aligned} [Again applying integration by parts] \begin{array}{r}\frac{1}{2}x^3 e^{2 x}-\frac{3}{4}x^2 \cdote^{2 x}+\frac{3}{2} \intx \cdote^{2 x} d x=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8}f(x)+c \\
\frac{1}{2}x^3 e^{2 x}-\frac{3}{4}x^2 \cdote^{2 x}+\frac{3}{2}\left[x \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}-\int1 \cdot \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}d x\right] \\
=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8}f(x)+c
\end{array} \begin{aligned}& \frac{1}{2}x^3 e^{2 x}-\frac{3}{4}x^2 e^{2 x}+\frac{3}{4}x e^{2 x}-\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{e^{2 x}}{2}=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8}f(x)+c \\
& \frac{e^{2 x}}{8}\left[4 x³-6 x²+6 x-3\right]+c_1=\frac{e^{2 x}}{8}f(x)+c
\end{aligned} $\therefore$ On comparison, we get f(x)=4 x³-6 x²+6 x-3 But given, \begin{aligned}& f(x)=1 \\
& 4 x³-6 x²+6 x-3=1 \\
& 4 x³-6 x²+6 x-4=0
\end{aligned} Divided by 2, we get \begin{array}{lr}& 2 x³-3 x²+3 x-2=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 2\left(x^3-1\right)-3 x(x-1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 2(x-1)\left(x^2+x+1\right)-3 x(x-1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & (x-1)\left[2 x²+2 x+2-3 x\right]=0 \\
\Rightarrow & (x-1)\left[2 x²-x+2\right]=0 \\
x=1 \text{ is real root. }
\end{array}$ So, sum of non-real complex root from the quadratic equation $2 x^2-x+2=0$ is $-\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)$=$\frac{1}{2}  Hence, option (a) is correct.$

19771.subject: Chemistry
19771.text:
On the basis of VSEPR theory, match the molecules listed in Column I with their shapes given in Column II.
No.Column INo.Column II
A$ClF_3$PSee-saw
B$BrF_5$QPentagonal bipyramidal
C$SF_4$RSquare pyramidal
D$IF_7$ST-shaped
19771.sol:
For $\mathrm{ClF_3}$, the central atom $\mathrm{Cl}$ has $7$ valence electrons. It forms $3$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $2$ lone pairs. The steric number is $3 + 2 = 5$, which corresponds to trigonal bipyramidal geometry. With $2$ lone pairs in equatorial positions, the shape is T-shaped. Thus, $\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{S}$.

For $\mathrm{BrF_5}$, the central atom $\mathrm{Br}$ has $7$ valence electrons. It forms $5$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $5 + 1 = 6$, which corresponds to octahedral geometry. With $1$ lone pair, the shape is square pyramidal. Thus, $\mathrm{B} = \mathrm{R}$.

For $\mathrm{SF_4}$, the central atom $\mathrm{S}$ has $6$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $4 + 1 = 5$, which corresponds to trigonal bipyramidal geometry. With $1$ lone pair in an equatorial position, the shape is see-saw. Thus, $\mathrm{C} = \mathrm{P}$.

For $\mathrm{IF_7}$, the central atom $\mathrm{I}$ has $7$ valence electrons. It forms $7$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $0$ lone pairs. The steric number is $7$, which corresponds to pentagonal bipyramidal geometry. Thus, $\mathrm{D} = \mathrm{Q}$.

Comparing these results, we have $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{S}$, $\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{R}$, $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P}$, and $\mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$

21121.subject: Mathematics
21121.text: The equation of the circle which touches the $x$-axis, passes through the point $(1,1)$ and whose centre lies on the line $x+y=3$ in the first quadrant is
21121.sol:
Let the centre of the circle be $(h, k)$. Since the circle touches the $x$-axis, the radius $r$ is equal to $|k|$. As the circle is in the first quadrant, $k > 0$, so $r = k$.

The centre $(h, k)$ lies on the line $x + y = 3$, so $h + k = 3$, which implies $h = 3 - k$.

The equation of the circle is $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = k^2$. Substituting $h = 3 - k$, we get $(x - (3 - k))^2 + (y - k)^2 = k^2$.

The circle passes through $(1,1)$, so $(1 - (3 - k))^2 + (1 - k)^2 = k^2$.

Simplifying the equation: $(k - 2)^2 + (1 - k)^2 = k^2$.

$k^2 - 4k + 4 + 1 - 2k + k^2 = k^2$.

$k^2 - 6k + 5 = 0$.

$(k - 1)(k - 5) = 0$.

If $k = 1$, then $h = 3 - 1 = 2$. The centre is $(2,1)$ and radius $r = 1$. The equation is $(x - 2)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 1^2$, which simplifies to $x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 - 2y + 1 = 1$, or $x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 2y + 4 = 0$.

If $k = 5$, then $h = 3 - 5 = -2$. This centre $(-2,5)$ is not in the first quadrant, so we discard this solution.

Answer: $x^2+y^2-4 x-2 y+4=0$

21526.text: Find the length of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(4,-7)$ to the line joining the origin and the point of intersection of the lines $2 x-3 y+14=0$ and $5 x+4 y-7=0$
21526.sol:
Let the two given lines be $L_1: 2x - 3y + 14 = 0$ and $L_2: 5x + 4y - 7 = 0$.

To find the point of intersection, multiply $L_1$ by 4 and $L_2$ by 3:
$8x - 12y + 56 = 0$
$15x + 12y - 21 = 0$

Adding these equations gives $23x + 35 = 0$, so $x = -\dfrac{35}{23}$.
Substituting $x$ into $L_1$: $2(-\dfrac{35}{23}) - 3y + 14 = 0 \Rightarrow -\dfrac{70}{23} + 14 = 3y \Rightarrow 3y = \dfrac{-70 + 322}{23} = \dfrac{252}{23} \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{84}{23}$.

The point of intersection is $P(-\dfrac{35}{23}, \dfrac{84}{23})$. The line joining the origin $(0,0)$ and $P$ has the equation $y - 0 = \dfrac{84/23 - 0}{-35/23 - 0}(x - 0)$, which simplifies to $y = -\dfrac{84}{35}x = -\dfrac{12}{5}x$.

Rearranging gives $12x + 5y = 0$.

The length of the perpendicular from $(4,-7)$ to $12x + 5y = 0$ is given by $d = \dfrac{|12(4) + 5(-7)|}{\sqrt{12^2 + 5^2}} = \dfrac{|48 - 35|}{\sqrt{144 + 25}} = \dfrac{13}{\sqrt{169}} = \dfrac{13}{13} = 1$.

Answer: 1 unit

21825.subject: Mathematics
21825.text:
A coach needs to select a 4 - player starting lineup from a pool of 10 players:
5 guards
3 forwards
2 centres
Find the number of different selections if the 4-player starting lineup must include:
At least 1 guard
At most 1 forward
Exactly 1 centre
21825.sol:
Let $g$, $f$, and $c$ be the number of guards, forwards, and centres selected respectively.

We are given the following conditions:
$g + f + c = 4$
$g \ge 1$
$f \le 1$
$c = 1$

Substituting $c = 1$ into the first equation, we get $g + f = 3$.

Since $f \le 1$, the possible values for $f$ are $0$ and $1$.

Case 1: $f = 0$
If $f = 0$, then $g = 3$. This satisfies $g \ge 1$.
The number of ways to select 3 guards, 0 forwards, and 1 centre is:
^{5}C_{3} \times ^{3}C_{0} \times ^{2}C_{1} = 10 \times 1 \times 2 = 20$

Case 2: $f = 1$
If $f = 1$, then $g = 2$. This satisfies $g \ge 1$.
The number of ways to select 2 guards, 1 forward, and 1 centre is:
^{5}C_{2} \times ^{3}C_{1} \times ^{2}C_{1} = 10 \times 3 \times 2 = 60$

Total number of different selections is the sum of the ways from both cases:
$20 + 60 = 80$

Answer: $80$

22294.text: Let $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$ be the position vectors of P and Q with respect to the origin. If points R and S divide PQ internally and externally in the ratio 2:3 respectively, then $\overrightarrow{OR}$ and $\overrightarrow{OS}$ are perpendicular when
22294.sol:
The position vector of point R dividing PQ internally in the ratio $2:3$ is given by:

$\overrightarrow{OR} = \dfrac{2\vec{q} + 3\vec{p}}{2 + 3} = \dfrac{3\vec{p} + 2\vec{q}}{5}$

The position vector of point S dividing PQ externally in the ratio $2:3$ is given by:

$\overrightarrow{OS} = \dfrac{2\vec{q} - 3\vec{p}}{2 - 3} = \dfrac{2\vec{q} - 3\vec{p}}{-1} = 3\vec{p} - 2\vec{q}$

Since $\overrightarrow{OR}$ and $\overrightarrow{OS}$ are perpendicular, their dot product must be zero:

$\overrightarrow{OR} \cdot \overrightarrow{OS} = 0$

$\left( \dfrac{3\vec{p} + 2\vec{q}}{5} \right) \cdot (3\vec{p} - 2\vec{q}) = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{5} \left( 9|\vec{p}|^2 - 4|\vec{q}|^2 \right) = 0$

$9|\vec{p}|^2 - 4|\vec{q}|^2 = 0$

$9|\vec{p}|^2 = 4|\vec{q}|^2$

Answer: $9\,|\vec{p}|^2 = 4\,|\vec{q}|^2$

22366.text: In a pure inductive circuit, a sinusoidal voltage $V(t)=200 \sin 250 t$ is applied to a pure inductance of $\mathrm{L}=0.02 \mathrm{H}$. The current through the coil is:
22366.sol:
The given voltage is $V(t) = 200 \sin(250t)$. Comparing this with $V(t) = V_m \sin(\omega t)$, we have $V_m = 200 \text{ V}$ and $\omega = 250 \text{ rad/s}$.

The inductive reactance $X_L$ is given by $X_L = \omega L$. Substituting the given values, $X_L = 250 \times 0.02 = 5 \Omega$.

The peak current $I_m$ is given by $I_m = \dfrac{V_m}{X_L} = \dfrac{200}{5} = 40 \text{ A}$.

In a pure inductive circuit, the current lags the voltage by a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Therefore, the expression for current $I(t)$ is $I(t) = I_m \sin \left(\omega$ t - $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).

Substituting the values, $ I(t) = 40 \sin $\left(250t - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

Answer: $40 \sin \left[250 t-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

22842.text: The force between two electric point charges at rest in air is $F_1$ When the same arrangement is kept inside water, the force between them is $F_2$. Which of the following statement is correct?
22842.sol:
The electrostatic force between two point charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ separated by a distance $r$ in a medium with dielectric constant $K$ is given by Coulomb's law as $F = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0 K} \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$.

In air, the dielectric constant $K_{air} \approx 1$. Thus, the force is $F_1 = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$.

In water, the dielectric constant $K_{water} \approx 80$. Thus, the force is $F_2 = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0 K_{water}} \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r^2} = \dfrac{F_1}{K_{water}}$.

Since $K_{water} > 1$, it follows that $F_2 < F_1$.

Answer: $F_2< F_1$

24365.subject: Physics
24365.text: Consider two Carnot engines of efficiencies $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$. The first engine absorbs heat $Q_1$ from a heat reservoir $A$ and releases heat $Q_2$ to a heat reservoir $B$. The second engine takes heat $Q_2$ from $B$ and releases heat $Q_3$ to a heat reservoir $C$. If $Q_1 > Q_2 > Q_3$, what is the net efficiency of this combination of the two Carnot engines?
24365.sol:
The efficiency of the first Carnot engine is given by $\eta_1 = 1 - \dfrac{Q_2}{Q_1}$.

This can be rewritten as $\dfrac{Q_2}{Q_1} = 1 - \eta_1$.

The efficiency of the second Carnot engine is given by $\eta_2 = 1 - \dfrac{Q_3}{Q_2}$.

This can be rewritten as $\dfrac{Q_3}{Q_2} = 1 - \eta_2$.

The net efficiency of the combination of the two engines is the total work done divided by the total heat absorbed from the source.

Total work done is $W = W_1 + W_2 = (Q_1 - Q_2) + (Q_2 - Q_3) = Q_1 - Q_3$.

The net efficiency is $\eta = \dfrac{W}{Q_1} = \dfrac{Q_1 - Q_3}{Q_1} = 1 - \dfrac{Q_3}{Q_1}$.

Multiplying the ratios of heat gives $\dfrac{Q_3}{Q_1} = \dfrac{Q_3}{Q_2} \times \dfrac{Q_2}{Q_1} = (1 - \eta_2)(1 - \eta_1)$.

Substituting this into the expression for net efficiency:

$\eta = 1 - (1 - \eta_1)(1 - \eta_2)$

$\eta = 1 - (1 - \eta_1 - \eta_2 + \eta_1\eta_2)$

$\eta = \eta_1 + \eta_2 - \eta_1\eta_2$

Answer: $\eta_1 + \eta_2 - \eta_1\eta_2$

25467.subject: Mathematics
25467.text:
Let $y = f(x)$ be the real valued function defined on the interval $(0, \infty)$, satisfying $y(1) = 0$ and the differential equation
$x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y - x^3$.
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: The function $f$ has a local minimum at $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
The function $f$ has a local maximum at $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
The function $f$ is increasing in the interval $(1, 2)$
If $g(x) = 4x^3 - 5x^2 + \dfrac{3}{2}x$ for $x > 0$, then the number of elements in the set $\{x \in (0, \infty) : f(x) = g(x)\}$ is $2$
25467.sol:
The given differential equation is $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y - x^3$.

Dividing by $x$, we get:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{x}y = -x^2$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)$, where $P(x) = -\dfrac{1}{x}$ and $Q(x) = -x^2$.

Integrating Factor (IF) = $e^{\int -\dfrac{1}{x} dx} = e^{-\ln x} = \dfrac{1}{x}$.

Multiplying the differential equation by the IF:
$\dfrac{d}{dx} \left( y \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} \right) = -x$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$:
$\dfrac{y}{x} = -\dfrac{x^2}{2} + C$
$y = -\dfrac{x^3}{2} + Cx$

Given $y(1) = 0$:
$0 = -\dfrac{1}{2} + C \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{2}$.

To find local extrema, we find $f'(x)$:
$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3x^2}{2}$

Setting $f'(x) = 0$ gives $3x^2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ (since $x > 0$).

Now, $f''(x) = -3x$. At $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, $f''\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\sqrt{3} < 0$.
So, $f(x)$ has a local maximum at $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

For $x \in (1, 2)$, $x^2 > 1$, so $f'(x) = \dfrac{1 - 3x^2}{2} < 0$. Thus, $f(x)$ is decreasing in $(1, 2)$.

For the intersection of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$:
$\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{2} = 4x^3 - 5x^2 + \dfrac{3}{2}x$
$x - x^3 = 8x^3 - 10x^2 + 3x$
$9x^3 - 10x^2 + 2x = 0$
$x(9x^2 - 10x + 2) = 0$

Since $x \in (0, \infty)$, $x \neq 0$. We solve $9x^2 - 10x + 2 = 0$.
Discriminant $\Delta = (-10)^2 - 4(9)(2) = 100 - 72 = 28 > 0$.
Sum of roots $= \dfrac{10}{9} > 0$ and Product of roots $= \dfrac{2}{9} > 0$.
Both roots are real and positive. Therefore, there are exactly $2$ elements in the set.

Answer: The function $f$ has a local maximum at $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$; If $g(x) = 4x^3 - 5x^2 + \dfrac{3}{2}x$ for $x > 0$, then the number of elements in the set $\{x \in (0, \infty) : f(x) = g(x)\}$ is $2$

28146.subject: Chemistry
28146.text:
The half-life of ${ }^{65} \mathrm{Zn}$ is 245 days. After $x$ days, $75 \%$ of original activity remained. The value of $x$ in days is $\_\_\_\_$. (Nearest integer)
(Given: $\log 3=0.4771$ and $\log 2=0.3010$)
28146.sol:
Using radioactive decay: $A = A_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/t_{1/2}}$.
With 75% activity remaining: $0.75 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x/245}$.
Taking log base 10: $\log(0.75) = \frac{x}{245}\log(0.5)$.
Calculate: $\log(0.75) = \log 3 - \log 4 = 0.4771 - 2(0.3010) = -0.1249$ and $\log(0.5) = -0.3010$.
Thus $-0.1249 = \frac{x}{245} \times (-0.3010)$, giving $x = \frac{0.1249 \times 245}{0.3010} = 101.66 \approx 102$ days (nearest integer).

30885.subject: Chemistry
30885.text:
Consider the following reactions
$\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{~B}_{4} \mathrm{O}_{7} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2 \mathrm{X}+$$\mathrm{Y}$$
$$\mathrm{CuSO}_{4}+$$\mathrm{Y}$ \xrightarrow{$\text{ Non-Luminous flame }$} $\mathrm{Z}+$$\mathrm{SO}_{3}$$
$2 $\mathrm{Z}+$2 $\mathrm{X}+$$ Carbon $\xrightarrow{$\text{ Luminous flame }$} 2 $\mathrm{Q}+\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{~B}_{4} \mathrm{O}_{7}+$$\mathrm{CO}$
The oxidation states of Cu in Z and Q, respectively are :
30885.sol:
The given reactions describe the Borax Bead Test.
When borax ($Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O$) is heated, it first loses water and then melts to form a transparent glassy bead consisting of sodium metaborate ($NaBO_2$) and boric anhydride ($B_2O_3$).
$Na_2B_4O_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2NaBO_2 (X) + B_2O_3 (Y)$
In the non-luminous (oxidizing) flame, $B_2O_3$ reacts with $CuSO_4$ to form copper(II) metaborate ($Z$), which is blue in color.
$CuSO_4 + B_2O_3 \xrightarrow{Non-Luminous} Cu(BO_2)_2 (Z) + SO_3$
In $Cu(BO_2)_2$, the oxidation state of $Cu$ is $+2$.
In the luminous (reducing) flame, the copper(II) metaborate is reduced by carbon to copper(I) metaborate ($Q$), which is colorless/red.
$2Cu(BO_2)_2 (Z) + 2NaBO_2 (X) + C \xrightarrow{Luminous} 2CuBO_2 (Q) + Na_2B_4O_7 + CO$
In $CuBO_2$, the oxidation state of $Cu$ is $+1$.
Therefore, the oxidation states of $Cu$ in $Z$ and $Q$ are $+2$ and $+1$ respectively.

In the following reaction, the total number of oxygen atoms in $X$ and $Y$ is______

${Na}_{2}O + {H}_{2}O \to 2X$

${Cl}_{2}{O}_{7} + {H}_{2}O \to 2Y$

Let's first balance the two given chemical equations:

${Na}_{2}O + {H}_{2}O ⟶ 2NaOH\left(X\right)$

In this equation, there are two $NaOH$ molecules, so the total number of oxygen atoms in the products is $1$.

${Cl}_{2}{O}_{7} + {H}_{2}O ⟶ 2{HClO}_{4}\left(Y\right)$

In this equation, there are two ${HClO}_{4}$ molecules, so the total number of oxygen atoms in the products is $4 .$

So $X$ has one $O$ and $Y$ has four $O$.

33184.text: The area (in sq. units) of the region bounded by the curves ${x}^{2} + 2y - 1 = 0, {y}^{2} + 4x - 4 = 0$ and ${y}^{2} - 4x - 4 = 0$ in the upper half plane is _________.
33184.sol:
The given curves are ${x}^{2} + 2y - 1 = 0, {y}^{2} + 4x - 4 = 0$ and ${y}^{2} - 4x - 4 = 0 .$

Drawing their graphs, we get

The required area is shown by the shaded part and since the curves ${y}^{2} + 4x - 4 = 0$ and ${y}^{2} - 4x - 4 = 0$ are symmetric about the $y$-axis, hence they have the same area.

Hence, the required area$= 2\left[{∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{4 - {y}^{2}}{4}\right)dy - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1 - {x}^{2}}{2}\right)dx\right]$

$= 2\left[{∫}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{1}{4}\left(4 - {y}^{2}\right)dy - {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)dx\right]$

$= 2\left[\dfrac{1}{4}{\left(4y - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{3}\right)}_{0}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right)}_{0}^{1}\right]$

$= 2\left[\dfrac{1}{4}\left(8 - \dfrac{8}{3} - 0\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3} - 0\right)\right]$

$= 2\left[\dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right] = 2sq . units$ .

33329.text: In the expansion of $\left(1 + x\right)\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right){\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}, x \ne 0$, the sum of the coefficient of ${x}^{3} and {x}^{- 13}$ is equal to ______
33329.sol:
Given,

$\left(1 + x\right)\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right){\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}$

$= {\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}\left(1 - x\right){\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3} + 3{x}^{2} + 3x + 1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}$

$= {\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}\left(1 - x\right){\left(\dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}$

$= \dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}\left(1 - x\right)}{{x}^{15}}$

$= \dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}}{{x}^{15}} - \dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}}{{x}^{14}}$

Now for coefficient of ${x}^{3}$, we will find coefficient of ${x}^{18}$ in expansion of ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which is not possible and ${x}^{17}$ in expansion of $- {\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which will be $- C17 17 = - 1$

And for coefficient of ${x}^{- 13}$ we will coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in expansion of ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which will be $C2 17$ and coefficient of $x$ in expansion of $- {\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which will be $- C1 17$, so the coefficient of ${x}^{- 13}$ will be $C2 17 - C1 17 = 136 - 17 = 119$

Hence, the sum will be $119 - 1 = 118$

33615.text: Let $C$ be the centre of the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - x + 2y = \dfrac{11}{4}$ and $P$ be a point on the circle. A line passes through the point $C$, makes an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the line $CP$ and intersects the circle at the points $Q$ and $R$. Then the area of the triangle $PQR$ (in ${unit}^{2}$) is
33615.sol:
Given,

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - x + 2y = \dfrac{11}{4}$

On rearranging terms we get,

$⇒ {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(y + 1\right)}^{2} = {\left(2\right)}^{2}$

Now given in $∆ PQR$, $∠ PCR = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ so $∠ PQR = 22\dfrac{1}{2}$ by circle property, radius is $2$ so $RC = QC = 2$

Now, $PR = QRsin22\dfrac{1}{2}$$= 4sin\dfrac{\pi}{8}$

And $PQ = QRcos22\dfrac{1}{2} = 4cos22\dfrac{1}{2}$

Now area of $\DeltaPQR = \dfrac{1}{2}PR \times PQ$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(4sin\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right)\left(4cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right)$

$= 4 \times \left(2sin\dfrac{\pi}{8}cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right)$

$= 4sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}$

33853.subject: Mathematics
33853.text: Let $S =${$z \in \mathbb{C}: \left|z - 3\right| \le 1$ and $z\left(4 + 3i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(4 - 3i\right) \le 24$}. If $\alpha + i\beta$ is the point in $S$ which is closest to $4i$, then $25\left(\alpha + \beta\right)$ is equal to ______.
33853.sol:
Given,

$\left|z - 3\right| \le 1$

Which represent a circle of radius $1$ and centred at $\left(3, 0\right)$

Now simplifying $z\left(4 + 3i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(4 - 3i\right) \le 24$

We get, $\left(x + iy\right)\left(4 + 3i\right) + \left(x - iy\right)\left(4 - 3i\right) \le 24$

$⇒ 4x + 3xi + 4iy - 3y + 4x - 3ix - 4iy - 3y \le 24$

$⇒ 8x - 6y \le 24$

$⇒ 4x - 3y \le 12$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Minimum distance of $\left(0, 4\right)$ from circle $= \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2}} - 1 = 4$ will lie along line joining $\left(0, 4\right) \text{ and } \left(3, 0\right)$
$∴$ equation line
$\dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{y}{4} = 1 ⇒ 4x + 3y = 12 \ldots \left(i\right)$
Equation of circle ${\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1 \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Solving (i) and (ii) we get,

${\left(\dfrac{12 - 3y}{4} - 3\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$

${\left(\dfrac{- 3y}{4}\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$

$\dfrac{25{y}^{2}}{16} = 1 ⇒ y = \pm \dfrac{4}{5}$

So, for minimum distance $y = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$∴ x = \dfrac{12}{5}$

$∴ 25\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = 25\left(\dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{12}{5}\right)$

$⇒ 16 \times 5 = 80$

34755.text: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3{x}^{2}y - y - 4{x}^{3}\right) = 0, x > 1$ with $y\left(2\right) = - 2$. Then $y\left(3\right)$ is equal to
34755.sol:
Given $x\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3{x}^{2}y - y - 4{x}^{3}\right) = 0$

$\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right)y = 4{x}^{3}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right)}{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}y = \dfrac{4{x}^{3}}{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$

Here $IF = {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{3{x}^{2} - 1}{x - {x}^{3}}dx}$

Let $x - {x}^{3} = t ⇒ IF = {e}^{∫ - \dfrac{dt}{t}}$

$= {e}^{- lnt} = \dfrac{1}{t}$

$∴ IF = \dfrac{1}{x - {x}^{3}}$

So the general solution of the differential equation will be

$y \times IF = ∫ Q \times IFdx$

$y\left(\dfrac{1}{x - {x}^{3}}\right) = ∫ \dfrac{4{x}^{3}}{x - {x}^{3}} \times \dfrac{1}{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{4{x}^{3}}{{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}^{2}}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{4x}{{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{2}}dx$

Now let $I = ∫ \dfrac{4x}{{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{2}}dx$

Substituting $1 - {x}^{2} = z$

$I = 2 ∫ \dfrac{- dz}{{z}^{2}}$

$= - 2\left(- \dfrac{1}{z}\right) + c = \dfrac{2}{1 - {x}^{2}} + c$

Hence the solution of the differential equation becomes

$\dfrac{y}{x - {x}^{3}} = \dfrac{2}{1 - {x}^{2}} + c$

At $x = 2, y = - 2$

$\dfrac{- 2}{2 - 8} = \dfrac{2}{1 - 4} + c$

$\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{- 2}{3} + c$

$∴ c = 1$

Hence the particular solution will be $\dfrac{y}{x - {x}^{3}} = \dfrac{2}{1 - {x}^{2}} + 1$

Put $x = 3$

$\dfrac{y}{3 - 27} = \dfrac{2}{1 - 9} + 1$

$\dfrac{y}{- 24} = - \dfrac{1}{4} + 1$

$- \dfrac{y}{24} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$y = \dfrac{3}{4}\left(- 24\right) = - 18$

34839.subject: Mathematics
34839.text: If $y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{2 x+1}{x}\right) y=e^{-2 x}, x>0,$ where $y(1)=\frac{1}{2} e^{-2},$ then:
34839.sol:
Given differential equation is,

$\frac{d y}{d x}+\left(2+\frac{1}{x}\right) y=e^{-2 x}, x>0$

$\mathrm{IF}=e^{\int\left(2+\frac{1}{x}\right) d x}=e^{2 x+\ln x}=x e^{2 x}$

Complete solution is given by

$y(x) \cdot x e^{2 x}=\int x e^{2 x} \cdot e^{-2 x} d x+c$

$=\int x d x+c$

$y(x) \cdot e^{2 x} \cdot x=\frac{x^{2}}{2}+c$

Given, $y(1)=\frac{1}{2} e^{-2}$

$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{2} e^{-2} \cdot e^{2} \cdot 1=\frac{1}{2}+c \Rightarrow c=0$

$\therefore \quad y(x)=\frac{x^{2}}{2} \cdot \frac{e^{-2 x}}{x}$

$y(x)=\frac{x}{2} \cdot e^{-2 x}$

Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$

$y^{\prime}(x)=\frac{e^{-2 x}}{2}(1-2 x)  < 0 \forall x \in\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$

Hence, $y(x)$ is decreasing in $\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$

35188.text: Let $A = { 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 }$. Then the number of possible functions $f: A \to A$ such that $f\left(m \cdot n\right) = f\left(m\right) \cdot f\left(n\right)$ for every $m, n \in A$ with $m \cdot n \in A$ is equal to
35188.sol:
Given,

$f\left(m \cdot n\right) = f\left(m\right) \cdot f\left(n\right)$

Taking $m = 1$

$⇒ f\left(1 \cdot n\right) = f\left(1\right) \cdot f\left(n\right)$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = 1$

Now taking $m = 3 \text{ and } n = 3$ we get,

$f ( 9 ) = f ( 3 ) \times f ( 3 )$,

So, $\left(f\left(3\right), f\left(9\right)\right)$ have two possibility $\left(1, 1\right) \text{ and } \left(3, 9\right)$

Now taking $m = 2 \text{ and } n = 1$ we get,

$f\left(2 \cdot 1\right) = f\left(2\right) \cdot f\left(1\right)$

Now here $f\left(1\right) = 1$, so $f\left(2\right)$ can take all $6$ numbers,

Similarly, for $f\left(5\right) \text{ and } f\left(8\right)$ there will be $6$ ways each,

So, total possible function will be, $= 1 \times 6 \times 2 \times 6 \times 6 \times 1 = 432$

35195.subject: Mathematics
35195.text: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function that satisfies the relation $f ( x + y ) = f ( x ) + f ( y ) - 1, ∀ x$, $y \in \mathbb{R}$. If ${f}^{'} ( 0 ) = 2$, then $| f ( - 2 ) |$ is equal to
35195.sol:
Given,

Functional equation $f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + f\left(y\right) - 1$

Now taking $x = 0 \text{$ and } y = 0 in above equation we get,

$f\left(0 + 0\right) = f\left(0\right) + f\left(0\right) - 1 ⇒ f\left(0\right) = 1$

Now we know that,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x + h\right) - f\left(x\right)}{h}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x\right) + f\left(h\right) - 1 - f\left(x\right)}{h}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(h\right) - 1}{h}$

Now let $\lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(h\right) - 1}{h} = k$

So, the equation becomes ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = k$

Now putting $x = 0$ in above equation we get,

${f}^{'}\left(0\right) = k ⇒ k = 2 \left\{\text{as given}{f}^{'}\left(0\right) = 2\right\}$

So, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2$

Now integrate both side we get,

$f\left(x\right) = 2x + c$

Now again taking $x = 0$ we get,

$f\left(0\right) = 2 \times 0 + c ⇒ c = 1\left\{\text{as}f\left(0\right) = 1\right\}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = 2x + 1$

And $f\left(- 2\right) = 2 \times \left(- 2\right) + 1 ⇒ f\left(- 2\right) = - 3$

Hence, $\left|f\left(- 2\right)\right| = 3$

Let $g: N \to N$ be defined as

$g: N \to N$

36827.text: A building construction work can be completed by two masons A and B together in 22.5 days. Mason A alone can complete the construction work in 24 days less than mason B alone. Then mason A alone will complete the construction work in :
36827.sol:
Let A take $a$ days and B take $a + 24$ days.
Together: $\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{a+24} = \frac{1}{22.5} = \frac{2}{45}$.
$\frac{2a+24}{a(a+24)} = \frac{2}{45}$
$45(2a+24) = 2a(a+24)$
$90a + 1080 = 2a^2 + 48a$
$a^2 - 21a - 540 = 0$
$(a-36)(a+15) = 0 \Rightarrow a = 36$.
Mason A alone completes the work in 36 days.

37886.subject: Mathematics
37886.text: If $\left(2\alpha+1, \alpha^2-3\alpha, \dfrac{\alpha-1}{2}\right)$ is the image of $(\alpha, 2\alpha, 1)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z}{1}$, then the possible value(s) of $\alpha$ is (are)
37886.sol:
Let the given point be $P = (\alpha, 2\alpha, 1)$ and its image be $P' = \left(2\alpha+1, \alpha^2-3\alpha, \dfrac{\alpha-1}{2}\right)$.

For $P'$ to be the image of $P$ in the given line $L: \dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z}{1}$, two conditions must be satisfied:
1. The midpoint of $P$ and $P'$ must lie on the line $L$.
2. The line segment $PP'$ must be perpendicular to the line $L$.

The midpoint $M$ of $P$ and $P'$ is:
$M = \left( \dfrac{\alpha + 2\alpha + 1}{2}, \dfrac{2\alpha + \alpha^2 - 3\alpha}{2}, \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{\alpha-1}{2}}{2} \right) = \left( \dfrac{3\alpha + 1}{2}, \dfrac{\alpha^2 - \alpha}{2}, \dfrac{\alpha + 1}{4} \right)$

Since $M$ lies on $L$, its coordinates must satisfy the equation of the line:
$\dfrac{\dfrac{3\alpha + 1}{2} - 2}{3} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\alpha^2 - \alpha}{2} - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{4}}{1}$

Simplifying the terms, we get:
$\dfrac{\alpha - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\alpha^2 - \alpha - 2}{4} = \dfrac{\alpha + 1}{4}$

Equating the first and third parts:
$\dfrac{\alpha - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\alpha + 1}{4}$

$2(\alpha - 1) = \alpha + 1 \Rightarrow 2\alpha - 2 = \alpha + 1 \Rightarrow \alpha = 3$

Substituting $\alpha = 3$ into the middle part to verify:
$\dfrac{3^2 - 3 - 2}{4} = \dfrac{4}{4} = 1$
The first and third parts also equal $1$, so $\alpha = 3$ satisfies the midpoint condition.

Now, let us check the perpendicularity condition. The direction ratios of $\overrightarrow{PP'}$ are:
$\left(2\alpha+1 - \alpha, \alpha^2-3\alpha - 2\alpha, \dfrac{\alpha-1}{2} - 1\right) = \left(\alpha+1, \alpha^2-5\alpha, \dfrac{\alpha-3}{2}\right)$

The direction ratios of the line $L$ are $(3, 2, 1)$. The dot product must be zero:
$3(\alpha+1) + 2(\alpha^2-5\alpha) + 1\left(\dfrac{\alpha-3}{2}\right) = 0$

Multiplying by 2 to clear the denominator:
$6(\alpha+1) + 4(\alpha^2-5\alpha) + (\alpha-3) = 0$

$6\alpha + 6 + 4\alpha^2 - 20\alpha + \alpha - 3 = 0$

$4\alpha^2 - 13\alpha + 3 = 0$

Factoring the quadratic equation:
$4\alpha^2 - 12\alpha - \alpha + 3 = 0$

$4\alpha(\alpha - 3) - 1(\alpha - 3) = 0$

$(4\alpha - 1)(\alpha - 3) = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{1}{4} \text{ or } \alpha = 3$

For $P'$ to be the image of $P$, both the midpoint and perpendicularity conditions must hold simultaneously. The only common value satisfying both conditions is $\alpha = 3$.

Answer: Only $3$

Statement I : When the frequency of an AC source in a series LCR circuit increases, the current in the circuit first increases, attains a maximum value and then decreases.

Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
38788.sol:
When an a.c. voltage is applied in a series LCR circuit, the current is increased first, attains a maximum and then decreases.

The formula to calculate the power factor is given by

$cosϕ = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{{R}^{2} + \left({{X}_{L}}^{2} - {{X}_{C}}^{2}\right)}} . . . \left(1\right)$

At resonance, ${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$, Hence,

$cos{ϕ}_{resonance} = 1$

Thus, both the statements are true.

39643.text:
With the help of potentiometer, we can determine the value of emf of a given cell. The sensitivity of the potentiometer is

(A) directly proportional to the length of the potentiometer wire

(B) directly proportional to the potential gradient of the wire

(C) inversely proportional to the potential gradient of the wire

(D) inversely proportional to the length of the potentiometer wire

Choose the correct option for the above statements:
39643.sol:
The basic principle of the potentiometer is that the potential drop across any section of the wire will be directly proportional to the length of the wire, provided the wire is of the uniform cross-sectional area and a uniform current flows through the wire.

Therefore, sensitivity of potentiometer wire is inversely proportional to potential gradient.

$Sensitivity ∝ \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{V}{l}} ∝ \dfrac{l}{V}$

42950.text: Two convex lenses of focal length $20cm$ each are placed coaxially with a separation of $60cm$ between them. The image of the distant object formed by the combination is at _____ $cm$ from the first lens.
42950.sol:
Let ${L}_{1}$ be the first lens and ${L}_{2}$ be the second lens.

The first refraction is in ${L}_{1}$.

Using lens formula,

${u}_{1} = \infty , {f}_{1} = 20cm, \dfrac{1}{{v}_{1}} - 0 = \dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} ⇒ {v}_{1} = 20cm$

Hence, the distance between the second image and the ${L}_{2}$ would be $\left(60 - 20\right) = 40cm$.

For the second lens ${L}_{2}$,

${u}_{2} = - 40cm, {f}_{2} = 20cm, \dfrac{1}{{v}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{u}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{{v}_{2}} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{20} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{{v}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{40} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 40cm$

So, the distance of image from first lens is

$x = 40cm + 60cm$

$= 100cm$

43216.text: Two discs of moment of inertia ${I}_{1} = 4kg{m}^{2}$ and ${I}_{2} = 2kg{m}^{2}$ about their central axes & normal to their planes, rotating with angular speeds $10rad{s}^{- 1} \text{ and } 4rad{s}^{- 1}$ respectively are brought into contact face to face with their axe of rotation coincident. The loss in kinetic energy of the system in the process is _________$J$.
43216.sol:
Applying conservation of angular momentum, we get

${I}_{1}{\omega}_{1} + {I}_{2}{\omega}_{2} = \left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right){\omega}_{0} ⇒ 4 \times 10 + 2 \times 4 = \left(4 + 2\right){\omega}_{0} ⇒ {\omega}_{0} = 8rad{s}^{- 1}$

Now, initial rotational kinetic energy is ${E}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{1}{\omega}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{2}{\omega}_{2}^{2} = 216J$

and final rotational kinetic energy is

${E}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right){\omega}_{0}^{2} = 192J$

Required, energy loss $\DeltaE = {E}_{1} - {E}_{2} = 24J$

A lead bullet penetrates into a solid object and melts. Assuming that $40 %$ of its kinetic energy is used to heat it, the initial speed of bullet is

$0 . 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = m{S}_{Pb}\left({T}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) + m{L}_{Pb}$

$0 . 2m{v}^{2} = m \times \left[125 \times \left(327 - 127\right) + 2 . 5 \times {10}^{4}\right]$

${v}^{2} = 5 \times \left[125 \times 200 + 2 . 5 \times {10}^{4}\right]$

${v}^{2} = 5 \times \left[25000 + 25000\right]$

$v = 500m{s}^{- 1}$

43720.text:
A geyser heats water flowing at a rate of $2 . 0kg$ per minute from $30 ° C$ to $70 ° C$. If geyser operates on a gas burner, the rate of combustion of fuel will be _____ $g{min}^{- 1}$.

[Heat of combustion $= 8 \times {10}^{3}{Jg}^{- 1}$, Specific heat of water $= 4 . 2{Jg}^{- 1}{C ∘}^{- 1}$]
43720.sol:
Given here, mass flow rate of water, $\dfrac{d m}{d t} = 2kg{min}^{- 1}$

The geyser heats the water, raising the temperature from ${\theta}_{1} = 30 ° C$ to ${\theta}_{2} = 70 ° C$.

Total heat utilised in raising the temperature, $\dfrac{\DeltaQ}{\Deltat} = \dfrac{d m}{d t} \times s\Delta\theta$

$\dfrac{\DeltaQ}{\Deltat} = \dfrac{2}{60} \times 4 . 2 \times 40 = \dfrac{m}{t} \times L$

$L =$ heat of combination$= 8 \times {10}^{3}J{g}^{- 1}$

Now, rate of consumption of fuel is $\dfrac{m}{t} = \dfrac{2 \times 4 . 2 \times 40}{60 \times 8 \times {10}^{3}}$

$= \dfrac{4 . 2}{6} \times {10}^{- 3} = 0 . 7 \times {10}^{- 3}kg{sec}^{- 1}$

$= 42g{min}^{- 1}$

44623.text: A small particle moves to position $5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ from its initial position $2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$ under the action of force $5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}N$. The value of work done will be ______ $J$.
44623.sol:
Work done by a constant force is given by $W = Force\left(\overset{\to}{F}\right) \cdot Displacement\left(\overset{\to}{r}\right)$, where, $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{r}2 - \overset{\to}{r}1$

Given here, $\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} = 5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{r}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

So, $W = \overset{\to}{F} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{r}2 - \overset{\to}{r}1\right)$

$= ( 5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot \left[( 5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) - ( 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k} )\right]$

$⇒ W = 40J$

47787.subject: Chemistry
47787.text: During the electrolysis of acidified water, $16$ g of $\text{O}_2$ gas is formed at anode. The volume of $\text{H}_2$ gas liberated at cathode under STP conditions is
47787.sol:
The overall reaction for the electrolysis of acidified water is:

$2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2$

Number of moles of $\text{O}_2$ produced $= \dfrac{16}{32} = 0.5$ mol

From the balanced chemical equation, $1$ mole of $\text{O}_2$ is produced for every $2$ moles of $\text{H}_2$.

Number of moles of $\text{H}_2$ produced $= 2 \times 0.5 = 1$ mol

At STP, the volume occupied by $1$ mole of an ideal gas is $22.4$ L.

Volume of $\text{H}_2$ gas liberated $= 1 \times 22.4 = 22.4$ L

Answer: $22.4$ L

55295.subject: Chemistry
55295.text: Which from following compounds has lowest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}$ value?
55295.sol:
Determining which compound has the lowest $\mathrm{pK}_\mathrm{b}$ value requires identifying the strongest base. A lower $\mathrm{pK}_\mathrm{b}$ corresponds to greater base strength.

Analyzing the compounds: Benzenamine is an aromatic amine where the nitrogen lone pair is resonance-delocalized into the ring, drastically reducing basicity and placing it as the weakest base. Ammonia serves as the reference base. Aliphatic amines, like propan-2-amine and N-ethylethanamine, are stronger bases than ammonia due to the electron-donating inductive effect of alkyl groups, which increases electron density on nitrogen.

Among aliphatic amines, the secondary amine N-ethylethanamine is stronger than the primary propan-2-amine. This results from the combined effects of two alkyl groups enhancing electron density and effective solvation of its conjugate acid in aqueous solution.

The order of basicity is N-ethylethanamine > propan-2-amine $ > \mathrm{NH}_3 > $ benzenamine. The strongest base, N-ethylethanamine, has the lowest $\mathrm{pK}_\mathrm{b}$.

55479.subject: Chemistry
55479.text: Which from following amino acids contains heterocyclic ring at a side chain $(\mathrm{R})$ group ?
55479.sol:
The presence of a heterocyclic ring in an amino acid side chain requires examining structural features beyond aliphatic or simple functional groups.

Threonine's side chain $\mathrm{-CH(OH)CH_3}$ is purely aliphatic with hydroxyl substitution. Cysteine's $\mathrm{-CH_2SH}$ contains a thiol group without cyclic structure. Valine's $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)_2}$ is a branched alkyl chain.

Histidine possesses an imidazole ring $\mathrm{-CH_2}$-imidazole as its side chain, featuring a five-membered aromatic heterocycle with two nitrogen atoms.

Only histidine contains a heterocyclic ring system, making it the correct identification.

60202.subject: Mathematics
60202.text: The number 28 is divided into two positive parts such that the sum of the cube of one part and the square of the other part is minimum, then the absolute difference between the two parts is
60202.sol:
Let the two positive parts of $28$ be $x$ and $28 - x$, where $0 < x < 28$.

Let $S$ be the sum of the cube of one part and the square of the other part. Then,

$S = x^3 + (28 - x)^2$

To find the minimum value of $S$, we differentiate $S$ with respect to $x$ and equate it to zero:

$\dfrac{dS}{dx} = 3x^2 + 2(28 - x)(-1)$

$\dfrac{dS}{dx} = 3x^2 + 2x - 56$

Setting $\dfrac{dS}{dx} = 0$, we get:

$3x^2 + 2x - 56 = 0$

$3x^2 + 14x - 12x - 56 = 0$

$x(3x + 14) - 4(3x + 14) = 0$

$(x - 4)(3x + 14) = 0$

Since $x$ must be positive, we have $x = 4$.

Now, we check the second derivative to confirm it is a minimum:

$\dfrac{d^2S}{dx^2} = 6x + 2$

At $x = 4$, $\dfrac{d^2S}{dx^2} = 6(4) + 2 = 26 > 0$, which confirms that $S$ is minimum at $x = 4$.

The two parts are $4$ and $28 - 4 = 24$.

The absolute difference between the two parts is $|24 - 4| = 20$.

Answer: $20$

60846.subject: Mathematics
60846.text: The equation $|z+1-i|=|z-1+i|$ represents a (where $z$ is a complex number)
options: Straight line passing through the origin and the first and third quadrant.
Straight line passing through the origin and the second and fourth quadrant.
Straight line passing through the point $(1,-1)$ and having slope -1.
Straight line passing through the point $(2,1)$ and having slope $\frac{1}{2}$.
60846.sol:
Let $z = x + iy$. The equation $|z+1-i| = |z-1+i|$ represents points equidistant from $-1+i$ and $1-i$.

Substituting $z = x + iy$ gives:

$|(x+1) + i(y-1)| = |(x-1) + i(y+1)|$

Squaring both sides eliminates the radicals:

$(x+1)^2 + (y-1)^2 = (x-1)^2 + (y+1)^2$

Expanding yields:

$x^2 + 2x + 1 + y^2 - 2y + 1 = x^2 - 2x + 1 + y^2 + 2y + 1$

Subtracting $x^2 + y^2 + 2$ from both sides simplifies to:

$2x - 2y = -2x + 2y$

Solving gives $4x = 4y$, so $x = y$.

The line $y = x$ passes through the origin and makes equal angles with the axes, lying in the first and third quadrants. Option A matches this result.

Option B corresponds to $y = -x$, option C describes a different line through $(1,-1)$ with slope $-1$, and option D is unrelated.

The final answer is A. It represents a straight line passing through the origin and the first and third quadrants.

62924.subject: Mathematics
62924.text: The logical statement $(p \vee q) \wedge [(\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)] \wedge \sim q$ is logically equivalent to...
62924.sol:
Given statement: $(p \vee q) \wedge [(\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)] \wedge \sim q$

Consider the part $[(\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)] \wedge \sim q$

Using distributive law:

$= ((\sim p \wedge q) \wedge \sim q) \vee ((p \wedge \sim q) \wedge \sim q)$

$= (\sim p \wedge (q \wedge \sim q)) \vee (p \wedge (\sim q \wedge \sim q))$

$= (\sim p \wedge F) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)$

$= F \vee (p \wedge \sim q)$

$= p \wedge \sim q$

Now, substitute this back into the original statement:

$= (p \vee q) \wedge (p \wedge \sim q)$

Using distributive law:

$= (p \wedge (p \wedge \sim q)) \vee (q \wedge (p \wedge \sim q))$

$= ((p \wedge p) \wedge \sim q) \vee (p \wedge (q \wedge \sim q))$

$= (p \wedge \sim q) \vee (p \wedge F)$

$= (p \wedge \sim q) \vee F$

$= p \wedge \sim q$

Answer: $p \wedge \sim q$

62944.subject: Mathematics
62944.text: Which of the following statements is logically equivalent to $\sim(p \leftrightarrow q)$ ?
62944.sol:
The logical equivalence of the biconditional statement is given by:

$p \leftrightarrow q \equiv (p \rightarrow q) \wedge (q \rightarrow p)$

Taking the negation of both sides:

$\sim(p \leftrightarrow q) \equiv \sim((p \rightarrow q) \wedge (q \rightarrow p))$

Using De Morgan's laws:

$\equiv \sim(p \rightarrow q) \vee \sim(q \rightarrow p)$

Since $p \rightarrow q \equiv \sim p \vee q$, we get:

$\equiv \sim(\sim p \vee q) \vee \sim(\sim q \vee p)$

Applying De Morgan's laws again:

$\equiv (p \wedge \sim q) \vee (q \wedge \sim p)$

Now, evaluating the expression $p \leftrightarrow \sim q$:

$p \leftrightarrow \sim q \equiv (p \rightarrow \sim q) \wedge (\sim q \rightarrow p)$

$\equiv (\sim p \vee \sim q) \wedge (q \vee p)$

Using the distributive law:

$\equiv (\sim p \wedge q) \vee (\sim p \wedge p) \vee (\sim q \wedge q) \vee (\sim q \wedge p)$

Since $\sim p \wedge p \equiv F$ and $\sim q \wedge q \equiv F$:

$\equiv (\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)$

Comparing the two results, we conclude that $\sim(p \leftrightarrow q) \equiv p \leftrightarrow \sim q$.

Answer: $p \leftrightarrow \sim q$

66804.subject: Physics
66804.text: The total charge induced in a conducting loop when it is moved in a uniform magnetic field depends on
options: the total change in magnetic flux.
the rate of change of magnetic flux.
66804.sol:
The induced charge in a conducting loop is determined by Faraday's law and Ohm's law. The induced electromotive force $E = -\frac{d\Phi}{dt}$ drives a current $I = \frac{E}{R} = -\frac{1}{R}\frac{d\Phi}{dt}$ through the loop.

Integrating this current over time gives the total charge: $q = \int I dt = -\frac{1}{R} \int d\Phi = -\frac{1}{R}(\Phi_f - \Phi_i)$.

Hence $|q| = \frac{|\Delta\Phi|}{R}$, showing that the total induced charge depends only on the net change in magnetic flux and the loop's resistance.

Final answer: $\boxed{C}$

69946.text: The heat energy that must be supplied to 14 gram of nitrogen at room temperature to raise its temperature by $48^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ at constant pressure is (Molecular weight of nitrogen $=28, R=$ gas constant, $C_p=\frac{7}{2} R$ for diatomic gas)
69946.sol:
Heat energy supplied at constant pressure is governed by $Q_p = n C_p \Delta T$, where $n$ is the number of moles, $C_p$ is molar specific heat at constant pressure, and $\Delta T$ is the temperature change.

For diatomic nitrogen, molar specific heat at constant pressure is $C_p = \frac{7}{2} R$. Given a mass of $14$ g and molecular weight $28$ g/mol, the number of moles is $n = \frac{14}{28} = 0.5$ mol. With $\Delta T = 48^{{}^{\circ}}\mathrm{C}$:

$Q_p = (0.5) \cdot \left(\frac{7}{2} R\right) \cdot 48 = 0.5 \cdot \frac{7}{2} \cdot 48 R = \frac{7}{4} \cdot 48 R = 7 \cdot 12 R = 84 R$.

The result is $84 R$, which corresponds to option B.

71350.text:
Match types of variation in column I with their causes in column II. Select the correct option.
Column IColumn II
A. Gene mutationI. occurs due to crossing over
B. Gene recombinationII. caused due to natural disasters
C. Gene flowIII. sudden permanent heritable change
D. Genetic driftIV. migration of organisms
71350.sol:
Gene mutation is a sudden, permanent, and heritable change in the genetic material.

Gene recombination occurs due to crossing over during the pachytene stage of meiosis I.

Gene flow is the transfer of genetic variation from one population to another, which occurs due to the migration of organisms.

Genetic drift is the change in the frequency of an existing gene variant in a population due to random chance events, often caused by natural disasters (bottleneck effect).

Thus, A matches with III, B matches with I, C matches with IV, and D matches with II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

71412.text: ZIFT, an assisted reproductive technology, is transfer of ________.
options: ovum collected from the donor to fallopian tube of the another female.
embryo into the uterus of the female.
externally fertilized ovum to the fallopian tube of the female.
sperms directly into the fallopian tube of female.
71412.sol:
ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer.

In this technique, the ovum is fertilized externally (in vitro fertilization) to form a zygote. The zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is then transferred into the fallopian tube of the female to complete its further development.

Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female is called GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer).

Transfer of an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus is called IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer).

Answer: externally fertilized ovum to the fallopian tube of the female.

71743.subject: Chemistry
71743.text: Which of the following coordination compounds is not likely to show optical isomerism?
71743.sol:
Optical isomerism is generally shown by octahedral complexes that lack elements of symmetry (plane of symmetry, center of symmetry).

Let us analyze each complex:

Option (1): $[NiCl_2(en)_2]$ can exist in cis and trans isomeric forms. The cis form lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active. The trans form has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. Therefore, the complex as a whole can show optical isomerism.

Option (2): $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$ is an octahedral complex with three bidentate ligands. It lacks any plane or center of symmetry. Thus, it exists as a pair of non-superimposable mirror images (enantiomers) and shows optical isomerism.

Option (3): $[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$ is a typical example of a square planar complex. Square planar complexes contain a molecular plane of symmetry (the plane containing the metal ion and the four ligands). Because of this plane of symmetry, they do not show optical isomerism.

Option (4): $[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}$ is an octahedral complex similar to the first option. Its cis-isomer is optically active, while the trans-isomer is optically inactive. Therefore, it can show optical isomerism.

Thus, the square planar complex $[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$ is not likely to show optical isomerism.

71965.subject: Chemistry
71965.text: Potassium forms bcc unit cell structure with edge length of 522 pm. Find the radius of the potassium atom ?
71965.sol:
For a body-centered cubic (bcc) unit cell, the atoms touch each other along the body diagonal. The relationship between the edge length $a$ and the atomic radius $r$ is given by:

$4r = \sqrt{3}a$

$r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}a}{4}$

Given the edge length $a = 522$ pm.

Substituting the value of $a$:

$r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} \times 522}{4}$

$r = \dfrac{1.732 \times 522}{4}$

$r = 1.732 \times 130.5$

$r = 226.026$ pm

Rounding to the nearest integer, the radius of the potassium atom is $226$ pm.

Answer: 226 pm

72362.subject: Physics
72362.text: For two inputs A and B and output Y, the Boolean expression for NOR gate is
72362.sol:
A NOR gate is a combination of an OR gate followed by a NOT gate.

The Boolean expression for an OR gate with inputs $A$ and $B$ is $Y' = A + B$.

Passing this output through a NOT gate gives the final output $Y = \overline{Y'}$.

Therefore, the Boolean expression for a NOR gate is $Y = \overline{A + B}$.

Answer: $Y = \overline{A + B}$

76716.subject: Mathematics
76716.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^3, & x^2 < 1 \\ x^2, & x^2 \geq 1 \end{cases}$.

Consider the following statements:
I. The function is continuous at $x = -1$.
II. The function is differentiable at $x = 1$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76716.sol:
The given function can be rewritten as:

$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2, & x \leq -1 \\ x^3, & -1 < x < 1 \\ x^2, & x \geq 1 \end{cases}$

Checking continuity at $x = -1$:
Left Hand Limit (LHL) $= \lim_{x \to -1^-} x^2 = (-1)^2 = 1$
Right Hand Limit (RHL) $= \lim_{x \to -1^+} x^3 = (-1)^3 = -1$
Since LHL ≠ RHL, $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x = -1$. Statement I is incorrect.

Checking differentiability at $x = 1$:
First, check continuity at $x = 1$:
LHL $= \lim_{x \to 1^-} x^3 = 1$
RHL $= \lim_{x \to 1^+} x^2 = 1$
$f(1) = 1^2 = 1$
The function is continuous at $x = 1$.

Now, check the derivatives at $x = 1$:
Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= \lim_{x \to 1^-} \dfrac{d}{dx}(x^3) = \lim_{x \to 1^-} 3x^2 = 3(1)^2 = 3$
Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= \lim_{x \to 1^+} \dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2) = \lim_{x \to 1^+} 2x = 2(1) = 2$
Since LHD ≠ RHD, $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 1$. Statement II is incorrect.

Both statements are incorrect.

Answer: Neither I nor II

77990.subject: Mathematics
77990.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $X$ be a random variable following binomial distribution with parameters $n = 6$ and $p = k$. Further, $9P(X = 4) = P(X = 2)$.

What is the value of $P(X = 3)$?
77990.sol:
For a binomial distribution, the probability of $r$ successes is given by $P(X = r) = ^{n}C_{r} p^r q^{n-r}$, where $q = 1 - p$.

Given $n = 6$ and $p = k$, we have $q = 1 - k$.

The given condition is $9P(X = 4) = P(X = 2)$.

Substituting the probabilities, we get:

$9 \times ^{6}C_{4} k^4 (1-k)^2 = ^{6}C_{2} k^2 (1-k)^4$

Since ^{6}C_{4} = ^{6}C_{2} = 15$, we can cancel 15 k^2 (1-k)^2$ from both sides (as $k \neq 0$ and $k \neq 1$):

$9k^2 = (1-k)^2$

Taking the square root on both sides (since $k > 0$ and $1-k > 0$):

$3k = 1 - k$

$4k = 1 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Now, we need to find $P(X = 3)$:

$P(X = 3) = ^{6}C_{3} k^3 (1-k)^3$

$P(X = 3) = 20 \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^3 \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^3$

$P(X = 3) = 20 \times \dfrac{1}{64} \times \dfrac{27}{64}$

$P(X = 3) = \dfrac{540}{4096} = \dfrac{135}{1024}$

Answer: $\dfrac{135}{1024}$

78638.subject: Mathematics
78638.text:
For 10 observations on price ( $x$ ) and supply (y), the following data was obtained:
$\begin{aligned}
& \sum \mathrm{x}=130, \sum \mathrm{y}=220 \\
& \sum \mathrm{x}^2=2288, \sum \mathrm{y}^2=5506 \text{ and } \sum \mathrm{xy}=3467 .
\end{aligned}$
What is line of regression of y on x ?
78638.sol:
Line of regression of $y$ on $x$ is :
$\begin{aligned}
& \begin{aligned}
& y-\bar{y}=b_{y x}(x-\bar{x}) \\
& \bar{y}=\frac{\Sigma y}{n} ; \bar{x}=\frac{\Sigma x}{n} \Rightarrow \bar{y}=\frac{220}{10}=22 ; \bar{x}=\frac{130}{10}=13 \\
& b_{y x}=\mathrm{r} \cdot \frac{\sigma_y}{\sigma_x} \\
& \mathrm{r}=\frac{n \Sigma x y-(\Sigma x)(\Sigma y)}{\sqrt{\left[n \Sigma x^2-(\Sigma x)^2\right]\left[n \Sigma y^2-(\Sigma y)^2\right]}} \\
&=\frac{10(3467)-(130)(220)}{\sqrt{\left[(10 \times 2288)-130^2\right]\left[(10 \times 5506)-\left(220^2\right)\right]}} \\
& \mathrm{r}=0.962 \\
& \sigma_y=\sqrt{\frac{\Sigma y^2}{n}-\left(\frac{\Sigma y}{n}\right)^2} \Rightarrow \sigma_y=8.2 ; \sigma_x=7.73 . \\
& \Rightarrow b_{x y}=0.962 \times \frac{8.2}{7.73}=1.02
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow$ Line of regression of $y$ on $x$ is :
$\begin{gathered}
y-22=1.02(x-13) \\
\Rightarrow y=1.02 x+8.74
\end{gathered}$

79844.subject: Botany
79844.text:
Match the following with respect to meiosis

(a) Zygotene (i) Terminalization
(b) Pachytene (ii) Chiasmata
(c) Diplotene (iii) Crossing over
(d) Diakinesis (iv) Synapsis

Select the correct option from the following
79844.sol:
Prophase I:
Prophase in meiosis-I is typically longer and more complex than the prophase in meiosis II. Prophase I is subdivided into five phases, viz. Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis.

Leptotene:
• During this stage, the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope. The compaction of chromosomes continues throughout this phase.

Zygotene:
• Chromosomes start pairing together. This process is called synapsis. The paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes.
• Formation of synapsis is accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex.
• The synaptonemal complex by a pair of homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad.

Pachytene:
• Bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads, at this stage.
• Recombination nodules appear. These nodules are the sites at which crossing overtakes place between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.
• Exchange of genetic materials between two homologous chromosomes takes place during crossing over. This leads to the recombination of genetic materials on the two chromosomes.

Diplotene:
• Synapotnemal complex is dissolved at this stage.
• The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalent separate from each other; except at the site of crossing over.
• The X-shaped structures; thus formed; are called chiasmata.

Diakinesis:
• Chiasmata is terminated at this stage.
• Meiotic spindles are formed to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation.
• Nucleolus disappears and nuclear envelope breaks down by the end of diakinesis.

80797.subject: Chemistry
80797.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : Oxidation of $p$-nitrotoluene with acidic KMnO$_4$ gives an acid that is stronger than benzoic acid.
Statement-II : Reduction of $p$-nitrotoluene with Sn/HCl followed by neutralization gives an amine that is more basic than aniline.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
80797.sol:
Oxidation of $p$-nitrotoluene with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ oxidizes the methyl group to a carboxylic acid group, yielding $p$-nitrobenzoic acid. The $-\text{NO}_2$ group is an electron-withdrawing group ($-I$ and $-M$ effects), which stabilizes the conjugate base (carboxylate ion). Hence, $p$-nitrobenzoic acid is a stronger acid than benzoic acid. Statement-I is correct.

Reduction of $p$-nitrotoluene with $\text{Sn}/\text{HCl}$ reduces the nitro group to an amino group, yielding $p$-toluidine ($p$-methylaniline). The $-\text{CH}_3$ group is an electron-donating group ($+I$ and hyperconjugation effects), which increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom and stabilizes the conjugate acid. Hence, $p$-toluidine is more basic than aniline. Statement-II is correct.

Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.

Answer: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.

80947.subject: Chemistry
80947.text: $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is dipolar whereas $\mathrm{BeF}_2$ is not. It is because:
options: the electronegativity of $\mathrm{F}$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{O}$
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ involves hydrogen bonding whereas $\mathrm{BeF}_2$ is a discrete molecule
80947.sol:
Water $\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)$ is polar because of the bent shape of the molecule. The shape means most of the negative charge from the oxygen on side of the molecule and the positive charge of the hydrogen atoms is on the other side of the molecule. This is an example of polar covalent chemical bonding. However, because of linear shape, dipole moments cancel each other in $\mathrm{BeF}_2\left(\mathrm{~F}^{-} \leftarrow \mathrm{Be}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{F}\right)$ and thus, it is non-polar.

90175.text: If $Im\left(\dfrac{iz - 2}{z - i}\right) = - 1$, (where $z \in C, z \ne i$) represents part of a circle, then the radius (in units) of the circle is (here, $Im ( z )$ represents the imaginary part of the complex number $z )$
90175.sol:
Let, $z = x + iy$
$Im\left(\dfrac{i\left(x + yi\right) - 2}{x + iy - i}\right) = - 1$
$⇒ Im\left(\dfrac{- \left(y + 2\right) + ix}{x + i\left(y - 1\right)}\right) = - 1$
$⇒ Im\left(\dfrac{\left(- \left(y + 2\right) + ix\right)\left(x - i\left(y - 1\right)\right)}{{x}^{2} + {\left(y - 1\right)}^{2}}\right) = - 1$
$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + y - 2 = - {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2y - 1$
$⇒ 2{x}^{2} + 2{y}^{2} - y - 1 = 0$
$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - \dfrac{y}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} = 0$
$⇒$ radius of the circle is $\sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{3}{4}$
$= 0 . 75$

Flower is defined as modified dwarf shoot which is meant for sexual reproduction. It is characteristic feature of angiosperm.

The flowers are termed pedicellate if they possess stalks and sessile if they lack them. The flower may be described as complete if it bears all the floral parts and incomplete, when one or more floral parts are absent. Flowers are called bisexual if they bear both androecium and gynoecium. The unisexual flowers have either androecium or gynoecium. The unisexual flowers may be male flowers or female flowers. The male flower are also called staminate flowers as they have stamens only.

100917.subject: Physics
100917.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding a ball striking the ground and rebounding. List-I contains the percentage of kinetic energy lost during the collision, and List-II contains the corresponding ratio of the rebound velocity to the impact velocity ($v_f / v_i$).

List-I (Percentage of KE lost)List-II (Ratio $v_f / v_i$)
(A) $36\%$(I) $0.5$
(B) $51\%$(II) $0$
(C) $75\%$(III) $0.8$
(D) $100\%$(IV) $0.7$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
100917.sol:
Let initial kinetic energy be $K_i$ and final kinetic energy be $K_f$.

Since $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$, the velocity ratio is $\dfrac{v_f}{v_i} = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_f}{K_i}}$.

If $36\%$ of kinetic energy is lost, $64\%$ is retained. $\dfrac{K_f}{K_i} = 0.64 \Rightarrow \dfrac{v_f}{v_i} = \sqrt{0.64} = 0.8$. (A) matches (III).

If $51\%$ of kinetic energy is lost, $49\%$ is retained. $\dfrac{K_f}{K_i} = 0.49 \Rightarrow \dfrac{v_f}{v_i} = \sqrt{0.49} = 0.7$. (B) matches (IV).

If $75\%$ of kinetic energy is lost, $25\%$ is retained. $\dfrac{K_f}{K_i} = 0.25 \Rightarrow \dfrac{v_f}{v_i} = \sqrt{0.25} = 0.5$. (C) matches (I).

If $100\%$ of kinetic energy is lost, $0\%$ is retained. $\dfrac{K_f}{K_i} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{v_f}{v_i} = 0$. (D) matches (II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

For elastic collision, $e=1$, so that $\theta^{\prime}=\theta$ and $v^{\prime}=v$

103133.subject: Physics
103133.text: A circuit consists of a battery of EMF $18\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1\ \Omega$ connected in series with a resistor $R_1$. The other end of $R_1$ is connected to a parallel combination of two branches. The first branch has a resistor $R_2 = 2\ \Omega$. The second branch has a capacitor $C = 3\ \mu\text{F}$ in series with a resistor $R_3 = 5\ \Omega$. The circuit is completed by connecting the parallel combination back to the battery. If the steady-state charge on the capacitor is $18\ \mu\text{C}$, the value of the unknown resistance $R_1$ is:
103133.sol:
In steady state, the capacitor is fully charged and acts as an open circuit, so no current flows through the branch containing $R_3$ and $C$.

The potential difference across the capacitor is given by $V_C = \dfrac{Q}{C} = \dfrac{18\ \mu\text{C}}{3\ \mu\text{F}} = 6\text{ V}$.

Since there is no current through $R_3$, the voltage drop across $R_3$ is zero. Therefore, the potential difference across the entire parallel combination is equal to the voltage across the capacitor, which is $6\text{ V}$.

This same potential difference of $6\text{ V}$ appears across the first branch containing $R_2$. The current through $R_2$ is $I = \dfrac{V}{R_2} = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3\text{ A}$.

Since no current flows through the capacitor branch, this $3\text{ A}$ is the total current supplied by the battery. Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law to the outer loop:
$E - I r - I R_1 - V_{\text{parallel}} = 0$
$18 - 3(1) - 3 R_1 - 6 = 0$
$12 - 3 - 3 R_1 = 0$
$9 = 3 R_1$
$R_1 = 3\ \Omega$.

Answer: $3\ \Omega$

103712.subject: Physics
103712.text: A uniform wire of length $L$ carrying a steady current $I$ is first wound into a circular coil of $N_1$ turns, producing a magnetic dipole moment $M_1$. The same wire is then unwound and rewound into another circular coil of $N_2$ turns, producing a magnetic dipole moment $M_2$. If the ratio of their magnetic dipole moments $\dfrac{M_1}{M_2}$ is $4$, what is the ratio of their number of turns $\dfrac{N_1}{N_2}$?
103712.sol:
For a circular coil of $N$ turns made from a wire of length $L$, the radius $R$ is given by $L = N(2\pi R)$, which means $R = \dfrac{L}{2\pi N}$.

The magnetic dipole moment is $M = NIA = NI(\pi R^2)$.

Substituting $R$, we get $M = NI\pi\left(\dfrac{L}{2\pi N}\right)^2 = \dfrac{IL^2}{4\pi N}$.

This shows that for a fixed length of wire, the magnetic moment is inversely proportional to the number of turns ($M \propto \dfrac{1}{N}$).

Given $\dfrac{M_1}{M_2} = 4$, we have $\dfrac{N_2}{N_1} = 4$, which gives $\dfrac{N_1}{N_2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

Answer: $1:4$

103713.subject: Physics
103713.text: A toroid with a mean radius of $20\text{ cm}$ has $4000$ turns of wire wound on its core. If a steady current of $5\text{ A}$ is passed through the wire, what is the magnetic field inside the core of the toroid?
103713.sol:
Mean radius of the toroid, $R = 20\text{ cm} = 0.2\text{ m}$

Total number of turns, $N = 4000$

Current, $I = 5\text{ A}$

The magnetic field inside the core of a toroid is given by $B = \mu_0 n I$, where $n$ is the number of turns per unit length.

For a toroid, the length is its mean circumference, so $n = \dfrac{N}{2\pi R}$.

Substituting this into the formula gives:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{2\pi R}$

$B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 4000 \times 5}{2\pi \times 0.2}$

$B = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 20000}{0.2}$

$B = \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-3}}{0.2} = 20 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T} = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ T}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ T}$

104811.text:
Read the following statements:
(A) Volume of the nucleus is directly proportional to the mass number.
(B) Volume of the nucleus is independent of mass number.
(C) Density of the nucleus is directly proportional to the mass number.
(D) Density of the nucleus is directly proportional to the cube root of the mass number.
(E) Density of the nucleus is independent of the mass number.

Choose the correct option from the following options.
104811.sol:
Radius of nucleus is $R = {R}_{0}A\dfrac{1}{3}$, where, ${R}_{0} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 15}m$ and A is mass number of nucleus.

Thus, $R ∝ A\dfrac{1}{3}$

Volume of nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} ⇒ V ∝ {R}^{3} ⇒ V ∝ A$.

Now, the density of nucleus is given by $ρ = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{mA}{\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}_{0}^{3}A} = \dfrac{m}{\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}_{0}^{3}}$

Thus, density is independent of $A$.

Hence, only $\left(A\right)$ and $\left(E\right)$ are correct.
104811.meta: Read the following statements: (A) Volume of the nucleus is directly proportional to the mass number. (B) Volume of the nucleus is independent of mass number.

104848.subject: Physics
104848.text:
Match List I with List II for an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen atom.

List I (Physical Quantity)List II (Proportionality)
A. Orbital radiusI. $n^3$
B. Kinetic energyII. $n$
C. Time period of revolutionIII. $n^{-2}$
D. Angular momentumIV. $n^2$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - IV, B - I, C - III, D - II
A - II, B - III, C - I, D - IV
A - IV, B - III, C - I, D - II
A - II, B - I, C - III, D - IV
104848.sol:
According to Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom:

A. Orbital radius $r_n \propto n^2$

B. Kinetic energy $K_n = \dfrac{13.6}{n^2} \text{ eV} \propto n^{-2}$

C. Time period of revolution $T_n = \dfrac{2\pi r_n}{v_n}$. Since $r_n \propto n^2$ and $v_n \propto n^{-1}$, $T_n \propto \dfrac{n^2}{n^{-1}} = n^3$

D. Angular momentum $L_n = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi} \propto n$

Therefore, the correct match is A - IV, B - III, C - I, D - II.

Answer: A - IV, B - III, C - I, D - II

111929.subject: Chemistry
111929.text: What is the correct IUPAC name of the compound $CH_3-CH=C(OH)-C \equiv CH$, and what is the hybridization state of the carbon atom bearing the hydroxyl group?
111929.sol:
Step 1: Identify the principal functional group, which is the -OH group. The longest carbon chain containing the -OH group and the multiple bonds has 5 carbon atoms (root word: pent).

Step 2: Number the chain to give the principal functional group the lowest possible locant. Numbering from either left to right or right to left gives the -OH group position 3.

Step 3: Apply the lowest locant rule for the multiple bonds. Numbering from right to left gives multiple bonds positions 1 and 3. Numbering from left to right gives positions 2 and 4. The locant set (1, 3) is lower than (2, 4), so we must number from right to left.

Step 4: The suffixes for multiple bonds are arranged alphabetically. 'en' comes before 'yn'. The correct IUPAC name is pent-3-en-1-yn-3-ol.

Step 5: The carbon atom at position 3 is bonded to one -OH group (single bond), one carbon atom via a single bond, and one carbon atom via a double bond. It forms 3 sigma bonds and 1 pi bond, so its hybridization state is $sp^2$.

Answer: pent-3-en-1-yn-3-ol ; $sp^2$

111935.subject: Chemistry
111935.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Molecule)List-II (IUPAC Name)
(A) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$(I) Pent-1-en-4-yne
(B) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$(II) 2-Methylbuta-1,3-diene
(C) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$(III) But-1-en-3-yne
(D) $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$(IV) Pent-3-en-1-yne

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
111935.sol:
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules for compounds containing both double and triple bonds:
1. The parent chain is numbered to give the lowest locant set to the multiple bonds.
2. If there is a choice (tie), the double bond is given the lower number.

For (A) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$: Numbering from left gives locants 1,3. Numbering from right gives 1,3. Due to the tie, the double bond gets priority. Name: But-1-en-3-yne.

For (B) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$: Numbering from left gives 1,4. Numbering from right gives 1,4. Tie-breaker gives double bond priority. Name: Pent-1-en-4-yne.

For (C) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$: Numbering from right gives locants 1,3. Numbering from left gives 2,4. The lowest locant set is 1,3. Name: Pent-3-en-1-yne.

For (D) $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$: Numbering from left gives the methyl group the lower locant 2. Name: 2-Methylbuta-1,3-diene.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

117082.text: Which of the following statements regarding the highest oxides of $3d$ transition metals is incorrect?
options: $Mn_2O_7$ is an acidic oxide and is a covalent green oil at room temperature.
$CrO_3$ is a basic oxide that dissolves in dilute acids to give $Cr^{3+}$ ions.
$V_2O_5$ is amphoteric but predominantly acidic, and is widely used as a catalyst.
The highest oxidation number in the oxides of $3d$ metals coincides with their group number and is attained in $Sc_2O_3$ to $Mn_2O_7$.
117082.sol:
The statement in option 2 is incorrect. As the oxidation state of a metal increases, its ionic character decreases and its acidic character increases. In $CrO_3$, chromium is in its highest oxidation state ($+6$), making it an acidic oxide, not a basic one. It dissolves in water to give chromic acid ($H_2CrO_4$) and dichromic acid ($H_2Cr_2O_7$).

The other statements are correct facts from NCERT: $Mn_2O_7$ is a covalent green oil and is highly acidic. $V_2O_5$ is amphoteric but mainly acidic. The highest oxidation number in the oxides of the $3d$ series coincides with the group number and is attained in $Sc_2O_3$ to $Mn_2O_7$.

Answer: $CrO_3$ is a basic oxide that dissolves in dilute acids to give $Cr^{3+}$ ions.

117133.subject: Chemistry
117133.text: Which of the following periodic trends among transition elements is a direct consequence of lanthanoid contraction?
options: The atomic radii of 4d series elements are significantly larger than those of the corresponding 3d series elements.
The melting points of transition metals reach a maximum near the middle of each series.
The densities of 3d series elements are generally lower than those of the corresponding s-block elements.
The first ionization enthalpies of 5d series elements are generally higher than those of the corresponding 3d and 4d series elements.
117133.sol:
The lanthanoid contraction results in the 5d series elements having atomic radii very similar to those of the corresponding 4d series elements. However, the nuclear charge of 5d elements is higher by 32 units. Because the 4f electrons provide poor shielding, the effective nuclear charge acting on the outer valence electrons in 5d elements is significantly greater. As a result, the first ionization enthalpies of 5d elements are generally higher than those of the corresponding 3d and 4d elements.

Option 1 is true but is due to the addition of a new principal quantum shell.
Option 2 is true but is due to the maximum number of unpaired d-electrons contributing to strong metallic bonding.
Option 3 is a false statement; transition metals have higher densities than s-block elements.

Answer: The first ionization enthalpies of 5d series elements are generally higher than those of the corresponding 3d and 4d series elements.
